model_answer:
Lemonade's FY2024 results came in at or slightly above the full-year guidance it gave with Q3 results (October 30, 2024). Revenue and gross earned premium beat the range. Adjusted EBITDA loss and in force premium landed at the favorable edge of the range.

| Metric ($M) | Guidance given with Q3 2024 results | FY2024 actual | Versus guidance |
|---|---|---|---|
| In force premium (IFP) | $940–$944 | $943.7 | Within the range, at the top end |
| Gross earned premium | $823–$826 | $827.3 | Above the range |
| Revenue | $522–$524 | $526.5 | Above the range |
| Adjusted EBITDA loss | ($155)–($151) | About ($150) | Slightly better than the range |
| Stock-based compensation | About $64 | $64.5 | In line |
| Capital expenditures | About $10 | $9.4 | In line |

- **Guidance source:** In Q3, Lemonade raised full-year guidance for gross earned premium and revenue and reaffirmed guidance for all other metrics. That guidance was IFP of $940–$944 million, gross earned premium of $823–$826 million, revenue of $522–$524 million, and an adjusted EBITDA loss of ($155)–($151) million.
- **Implied Q4:** The Q3 guidance implied Q4 gross earned premium of $222–$225M, revenue of $144–$146M and adjusted EBITDA loss of ($29)–($25)M. Actual Q4 figures were better. Gross earned premium was $226.4M, revenue was $148.8M, and adjusted EBITDA loss was ($23.8)M.
- **Management's view:** The company said it delivered on its guidance "with notable precision," ending 2024 with IFP of $944 million, up 26% year over year, and an adjusted EBITDA loss of ($150) million, a 13% improvement.
- **Other results:**
  - Q4 gross loss ratio was 63%, the lowest on record.
  - Full-year gross profit nearly doubled to $167 million.
  - Full-year net loss was $202.2M, compared with $236.9M in 2023.
  - Adjusted free cash flow was $48 million, the first positive full year.

The FY2024 actuals come from Lemonade's Q4 2024 shareholder letter, and the Q3 guidance comes from its Q3 2024 shareholder letter. The "about ($150) million" adjusted EBITDA figure is the rounded number the company cites. I didn't pull the exact unrounded full-year figure.
